results.title: What is Endpoint Formula?, Examples
results.content: Let M (\((x)\_{m}\) , \((y)\_{m}\)) be a midpoint for the line joining two endpoints A (\((x)\_{1}\) , \((y)\_{1}\)) and B (\((x)\_{2}\) , \((y)\_{2}\)). Given the coordinates of M and A, the coordinates of B can be calculated using the following formula: \((x)\_{m}\)= \( \dfrac{x\_1 + x\_2}{2} \), \((y)\_{m}\) = \( \dfrac{y\_1 + y\_2}{2} \) \((x)\_{2}\) = 2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\), \((y)\_{2}\) = 2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\) Thus, the endpoint formula is, **Endpoint formula of B(\((x)\_{2}\), \((y)\_{2}\)) = (2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\),  2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\))** **Note:** It is not recommended to learn this formula, rather just find the coordinates of B by just using the midpoint formula. ### Endpoint Formula By solving the midpoint formula for the points x2 and y2, we get the endpoint formula, i.e. Endpoint formula of B(\((x)\_{2}\), \((y)\_{2}\)) = (2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\),  2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\)) Book a Free Trial Class ## Examples Using Endpoint Formula **Example 1: M(3, 4) is the midpoint of the line joining points A(5, 2) and B(x, y). \((x)\_{m}\) = 7, \((x)\_{1}\) = 3, \((y)\_{m}\) = 8, \((y)\_{1}\) = 5 \((x)\_{2}\) = 2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\) \((x)\_{2}\) = 2 × 7 - 3 \((y)\_{2}\) = 2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\) \((y)\_{2}\) = 2 × 8 - 5 Therefore, the coordinates of the other endpoint E(x, y) is (11, 11) **Example 3: P(5, 8) is the midpoint of the line joining points A(4, 3) and B(x, y). Let M (\((x)\_{m}\) , \((y)\_{m}\)) be a midpoint for the line joining two endpoints A (\((x)\_{1}\) , \((y)\_{1}\)) and B (\((x)\_{2}\) , \((y)\_{2}\)). Given the coordinates of M and A, the coordinates of B can be calculated using the following formula: \((x)\_{m}\)= \( \dfrac{x\_1 + x\_2}{2} \), \((y)\_{m}\) = \( \dfrac{y\_1 + y\_2}{2} \) \((x)\_{2}\) = 2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\), \((y)\_{2}\) = 2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\) Thus, the endpoint formula is, Endpoint formula of B(\((x)\_{2}\), \((y)\_{2}\)) = (2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\),  2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\)) ### What is the Midpoint Formula for Calculating the Endpoints? The endpoints can be calculated by using the midpoint formula: \((x)\_{m}\)= \( \dfrac{x\_1 + x\_2}{2} \), \((y)\_{m}\) = \( \dfrac{y\_1 + y\_2}{2} \) \((x)\_{2}\) = 2\((x)\_{m}\)- \((x)\_{1}\), \((y)\_{2}\) = 2\((y)\_{m}\)- \((y)\_{1}\) ### Using the Endpoint Formula, Calculate the Coordinates of B with S(10, 7) being the Midpoint of the Line Joining Points A(7, 4) and B(x, y).
